name: Contact lens hygiene break
summary: Pausing lens wear and cleaning properly is aimed at fewer red eyes; no study tests it for looks.
lead: A contact lens hygiene break refers to pausing contact lens wear and following careful lens hygiene to reduce eye redness. It appears in looksmaxxing lists as a way to get fewer red eyes.

name: Chest resonance training
summary: Speaking 'from the chest' for a deeper voice; acoustics sources say the chest adds little resonance, and no appearance trials exist.
lead: Chest resonance training is a looksmaxxing-adjacent voice practice in which a person tries to speak "from the chest" in order to produce a deeper, fuller-sounding voice. The phrase is also used in singing instruction, where teachers have long described a "chest voice" and the sensation of vibration in the upper torso.

name: Lowering pitch exercises
summary: Practising a lower speaking pitch for a deeper voice; physiology sets limits and no appearance trials exist.
lead: Lowering pitch exercises are vocal practices that people use to speak at a lower fundamental frequency, usually to sound deeper or more masculine. They appear in looksmaxxing discussion of voice as a way to change a perceived trait without surgery or drugs.

name: Vocal fry and glottal control
summary: Using creaky low-register phonation for a lower sound; perception studies exist but none test it for looks.
lead: Vocal fry, also called creaky voice or glottal fry, is the lowest vocal register, produced with loose glottal closure that yields a slow, popping or rattling sound at very low frequency. In looksmaxxing voice discussion, some people try to control it to make their voice sound lower.

name: Diaphragmatic breathing
summary: Belly breathing for breath support and a deeper voice; studied for stress and lungs, not for voice appearance.
lead: Diaphragmatic breathing, also called belly or abdominal breathing, is a technique that uses the diaphragm to take deep breaths, typically by inhaling slowly through the nose and exhaling through pursed lips. It is used in respiratory care, in stress and anxiety management, and in voice training, where it is associated with breath support.

name: Voice coach / speech therapy
summary: Professional voice therapy or coaching to change how a voice sounds; real clinical field, but no appearance trials.
lead: Voice coaching and speech therapy refer to professional services used to change how a voice sounds or functions. Voice therapy is provided mainly by speech-language pathologists, who target vocal parameters such as vocal fold closure, pitch, volume and quality, chiefly to manage voice disorders, but also to change overall voice quality, as in transgender voice therapy. Vocal pedagogy, taught by voice teachers, is the related field focused on singing.

name: Singing lessons
summary: Lessons in vocal technique for control and range; studied for wellbeing and lungs, not for changing how your voice looks or sounds in speech.
lead: Singing lessons are instruction in vocal technique from a voice teacher, covering breath support, phonation, resonance, articulation and range. In looksmaxxing culture they are mentioned as a way to gain voice control and range, including a deeper or more resonant speaking voice.

name: Humming exercises
summary: Closed-mouth humming used as a vocal warm-up; popular in voice-training circles, with little appearance-specific research.
lead: A hum is a wordless tone produced with the mouth closed, so the sound passes through the nose. In looksmaxxing and voice-improvement discussions, humming exercises are described as a vocal warm-up: a way to start phonation gently before speaking or singing.

name: Straw phonation
summary: Voicing through a narrow straw, a voice-therapy exercise with real clinical research, though not tested for vocal attractiveness.
lead: Straw phonation is an exercise in which a person produces voiced sound through a narrow straw or tube. It is one of several semi-occluded vocal tract (SOVT) exercises, which partly obstruct the mouth opening during phonation, and its use in voice training and therapy has grown over roughly two decades.

name: Resonance tuning (formant)
summary: Shaping vocal tract resonances (formants) to change vocal timbre; grounded in voice acoustics, untested as a looksmaxxing practice.
lead: Formants are broad peaks in the sound spectrum arising from acoustic resonance in the vocal tract; they shape the sound produced by the voice but are not sound sources themselves. Resonance tuning is the deliberate adjustment of the vocal tract to move these resonances, and it is discussed in voice-improvement communities as a way to change vocal timbre.

name: Pitch tracking apps
summary: Apps that read your voice's fundamental frequency in Hz; useful as a meter, with no studies behind appearance claims.
lead: Pitch tracking apps are smartphone or desktop programs that estimate the fundamental frequency (f0) of a recorded or live voice and display it in hertz or as a musical note. In voice-related appearance and presentation communities they are used to check how high or low a speaking voice sits, for example when practising a deeper or more resonant voice.

name: Testosterone replacement therapy
summary: Medical testosterone for low levels; can deepen voice via virilization, studied for muscle and metabolic outcomes in hypogonadal men.
lead: Testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) is the medical supplementation of testosterone to restore normal levels in people with hypogonadism, mainly men. It can be given by injection, gel, patch, pellet or oral forms.

name: Testosterone cypionate
summary: Long-acting injectable testosterone; labelled for hypogonadism, with voice deepening among its listed virilizing effects.
lead: Testosterone cypionate is a long-acting injectable ester of testosterone, sold mainly as Depo-Testosterone, and a prodrug the body converts to testosterone. It is FDA-labelled for replacement therapy in males with primary or hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

name: Anavar / oxandrolone voice risk
summary: Mild-reputation oral steroid whose documented risks in women include voice deepening that can be irreversible.
lead: Oxandrolone, sold as Oxandrin and colloquially known as Anavar, is an oral synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid. Its article lists voice deepening among the virilizing effects in women, and states that such masculinizing changes can be irreversible.

name: Anabolic steroids for voice
summary: Androgens can deepen the voice, but it is a side effect of virilization, not a studied use, and some changes may be irreversible.
lead: Anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) are synthetic androgens that, like testosterone, can lower the voice by acting on the larynx. Voice deepening is listed among the virilizing effects of testosterone and its esters, and in women it is reported as a possible effect of androgens.

name: HCG and clomiphene for voice
summary: Two fertility drugs that raise testosterone, floated for voice depth; no voice evidence exists.
lead: In looksmaxxing discussion, human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) and clomiphene (clomifene) are two prescription drugs sometimes mentioned as ways of raising endogenous testosterone, with the idea that higher testosterone could deepen or maintain a lower voice. Both are used medically for fertility and, off-label, for male hypogonadism.

name: Tongue posture for voice
summary: Applying mewing to the voice; the base practice is unproven and no voice study exists.
lead: Tongue posture for voice is the idea, circulated in looksmaxxing communities, that holding the tongue against the roof of the mouth, as in "mewing", changes vocal resonance. It extends the mewing claim, which concerns jaw and facial structure, to the sound of the voice.

name: Throat singing practice
summary: Traditional overtone vocal techniques repurposed for lower voice; effect on speech untested.
lead: Throat singing practice, in looksmaxxing and voice-training discussion, refers to using overtone or throat-singing techniques, such as Tuvan kargyraa or Tibetan chant, to train a lower or more resonant voice. Overtone singing is a traditional vocal technique in which a singer shapes the vocal tract so that selected harmonics stand out, producing two audible pitches at once.

name: Vocal cord filler injection
summary: A clinical procedure that bulks a weak vocal fold; evidence is for medical voice disorders, not cosmetic use.
lead: Vocal cord filler injection, medically called injection laryngoplasty or injection augmentation, places material into a vocal fold to add bulk and move it toward the midline so the folds meet better. It is used clinically for vocal fold paralysis and weakness, and appearance-focused communities discuss it as a way to restore a fuller voice.

name: Laryngoplasty / Adam's apple surgery
summary: Surgery that shaves down the Adam's apple; usually satisfied patients, rare vocal fold risk.
lead: Chondrolaryngoplasty, popularly called a tracheal shave, reduces the thyroid cartilage that forms the Adam's apple. The nickname is a misnomer because the trachea is not involved.

name: Voice surgery (cricothyroid approximation)
summary: Surgery that tightens the vocal folds to raise pitch; largely superseded and can leave a falsetto voice.
lead: Cricothyroid approximation (CTA) is a voice surgery that raises pitch by moving the cricoid and thyroid cartilages closer together, tensioning and lengthening the vocal folds. It has mainly been used for voice feminisation in transgender women.

name: Adam's apple enhancement
summary: Surgical enlargement of the Adam's apple, documented mostly in transmasculine facial masculinization; evidence is a handful of small case series.
lead: Adam's apple enhancement, sometimes called laryngeal or tracheal augmentation, is a surgical procedure that enlarges the visible laryngeal prominence at the front of the neck, which is typically more pronounced in men.  It is described in the medical literature mainly as one component of facial masculinization surgery for transmasculine patients, alongside mandible angle and chin procedures.

name: Neck training for voice
summary: The idea that thicker neck muscles lower your voice; no studies have tested it.
lead: Neck training for voice refers to the belief, circulating in looksmaxxing communities, that strengthening or thickening neck muscles can deepen the voice. No published studies examining this claim were found.

name: Hydration and humidifier for voice
summary: Drinking water and humidifying the room to keep vocal folds moist; studied only loosely, and humidifiers need upkeep.
lead: Hydration and humidifier use for the voice is a set of practices, drinking water and humidifying room air, that people adopt in the belief that moist vocal folds work better and recover faster. A study of karaoke singers examined hydration together with vocal rest in relation to vocal fatigue.

name: Throat coat tea
summary: Slippery-elm-style herbal teas for a soothed throat; traditional use, no trials.
lead: Throat Coat tea refers to herbal teas sold for throat comfort, commonly built around slippery elm, a plant whose inner bark has long been used in folk medicine for sore throat and sold in the US as an over-the-counter demulcent.  Singers and voice-conscious communities use such teas for soothing. No clinical studies of these teas were found.

name: Honey and ginger throat soothing
summary: Honey and ginger drinks for a sore throat; traditional, with some cough data for honey and little else.
lead: Honey and ginger throat soothing is a folk remedy of taking honey, ginger or both in warm drinks for throat comfort. A Cochrane review cited on Wikipedia found no strong evidence for or against honey for coughs, while the WHO recommends honey for coughs and sore throats.  Ginger has a long traditional medicine history, but its effectiveness for treating disease remains uncertain.

name: Vocal rest
summary: Resting the voice after strain; studied within the wider vocal-fatigue literature.
lead: Vocal rest is the practice of limiting or stopping speaking and singing to let the voice recover from strain. It is discussed in vocal hygiene guidance for voice professionals.  Research has examined vocal fatigue and recovery in singers and speakers.

name: Avoiding whispering
summary: A voice-care habit of speaking softly instead of whispering; the claim rests on limited and indirect evidence.
lead: Avoiding whispering is a voice-care habit in which a person speaks softly in a normal, voiced manner instead of whispering when trying to rest or protect the voice. It is discussed in appearance-related voice improvement as part of reducing vocal strain.

name: Treating acid reflux for voice
summary: Reflux control as a route to a clearer voice; LPR treatment evidence is mixed and the diagnosis is debated.
lead: Treating acid reflux for voice refers to managing laryngopharyngeal reflux (LPR), sometimes called silent reflux, with the aim of relieving hoarseness and improving voice quality. LPR is the backward flow of stomach contents into the larynx, oropharynx or nasopharynx.

name: Quit smoking for voice
summary: Stopping smoking to protect the voice; smoking is a documented cause of vocal fold swelling and hoarseness.
lead: Quitting smoking for voice refers to stopping tobacco use to avoid or reverse smoking-related voice changes such as hoarseness and a lowered, rougher pitch.
